title_en: Belief in the Divine Decree and Steadfastness in Times of Trial
body_ar: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا من يهده الله فلا مضل ومن يضلل فلا هادي له ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا) (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا (70) يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمَالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فَازَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا)
body_en:
All praise belongs to God. We praise Him and seek His help, and we take refuge in God from the evil of our own selves and from our evil deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — may God bless him, his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{O people, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women. Be mindful of God, in whose name you make demands of one another, and of the ties of kinship. God is ever watching over you.} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1)

{O you who believe, be mindful of God and speak with words that are true and sound (70). He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great triumph.} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71)
translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.

The page reproduces only the opening invocation (the khuţbat al-ḥājah) with its two customary verses. Nothing of the Sheikh's treatment of the divine decree (qadar) or of steadfastness under trial is present in the written source; the title is the only guide to the content.
As in article 496, the first invocation reads فلا مضل without the pronoun له; the sense is unaffected.
The verse markers '(70)' inside the second quotation are in the Arabic source and have been kept.
